units.source_text: 夜色渐深，冷风侵肌，十九夜的月亮才从云间出现。

en.t: The night deepened, a cold wind pierced the skin, and only then did the nineteenth-night moon appear from among the clouds.

units.source_text: 源氏对夕雾言道：“月色朦胧的春夜，真教人徒唤奈何啊！

en.t: Genji said to Yugiri, “A spring night with hazy moonlight truly leaves one helplessly sighing.

units.source_text: 然而秋夜也很可爱，像今天这种音乐演奏，如果与秋虫之声相应和，定然更多清趣，似觉音乐之声更加美妙了。”

en.t: Yet autumn nights are lovely too; music like tonight’s, if it mingled with the voices of autumn insects, would surely gain an even purer charm and seem all the more beautiful.”

units.source_text: 夕雾答道：“秋夜月色清光皎洁，洞烛万物，琴笛之音亦分外清澄。

en.t: Yugiri replied, “On an autumn night the moon shines clear and bright, illuminating everything, and the sounds of zithers and flutes become especially limpid.

units.source_text: 然而夜色过分明亮，有如人工造作，使人分心注目于种种秋花秋草、白露清霜，不能凝神听乐，亦是一大缺憾。

en.t: But when the night is too bright, it seems almost artificial, and one’s attention is drawn away to the autumn flowers and grasses, the white dew and clear frost, so that one cannot concentrate on the music; that too is a great flaw.

units.source_text: 春夜云霞弥漫天空，露出朦胧淡月，照着笙管合奏，其音节之清艳，实在无以复加！

en.t: On a spring night, clouds and mist fill the sky and a pale, hazy moon appears, shining on an ensemble of sho and pipes; the pure elegance of those tones could not be surpassed.

units.source_text: 古人说女子爱春天，良有以也。

en.t: When the ancients said that women love spring, they truly had good reason.

units.source_text: 故欲求音乐之调和美满，莫如于春日夕暮演奏。”

en.t: Therefore, if one seeks perfect harmony and fullness in music, nothing is better than performing at spring dusk.”

units.source_text: 源氏说：“否否，欲评春秋之优劣，谈何容易！

en.t: Genji said, “No, no. To judge whether spring or autumn is superior is hardly easy.

units.source_text: 从古以来，此事难于判定。

en.t: Since ancient times this matter has been difficult to decide.

units.source_text: 末世人心浅薄，岂能贸然作出结论！

en.t: In these latter days, when people’s hearts are shallow, how could one rashly draw a conclusion?

units.source_text: 惟音乐的曲调，向来春天的吕调为先，秋天的律调为次，果然自有其道理。”

en.t: Only in musical modes has it long been held that the ryo mode of spring comes first and the ritsu mode of autumn second, and there is indeed reason in that.”

units.source_text: 后来又说：“只有一事真不可解：现今大名鼎鼎的音乐专家，常常在御前演奏，但杰出之人日渐稀少。

en.t: Later he said again, “There is only one thing I truly cannot understand: the famous musicians of the present often perform before His Majesty, yet outstanding people grow fewer day by day.

units.source_text: 自命为老前辈的名手，毕竟学得多少本领呢？

en.t: Those celebrated masters who call themselves old veterans, how much skill have they really learned?

units.source_text: 教他们参与在这些并非专家的妇女中演奏，怕不见得特别优异吧。

en.t: If they were made to perform among these women, who are not specialists, I doubt they would seem especially superior.

units.source_text: 不过我自己年来离群索居，或许耳朵有些变乖了，真乃遗憾之事。

en.t: Still, I myself have lived apart from society for years, so perhaps my ears have become somewhat perverse, which is truly regrettable.

units.source_text: 说也奇怪，在这六条院里，无论学问或雕虫小技，一学即会的聪明人很多呢。

en.t: Strangely enough, here in the Rokujo estate there are many clever people who master whatever they study at once, whether learning or some small accomplishment.

units.source_text: 御前奏乐时被选为第一流名手的人，和这里的妇人们比较起来，孰优孰劣呢？”

en.t: If those chosen as first-rate masters for court performances were compared with the women here, which side would prove better?”

units.source_text: 夕雾说：“儿子也想谈论此事，只因自己缺乏修养，不敢信口雌黄。

en.t: Yugiri said, “I too would like to discuss this matter, but because my own cultivation is lacking, I dare not speak carelessly.

units.source_text: 世人恐怕是不曾听见过古代音乐之故吧，都把柏木卫门督的和琴和萤兵部卿亲王的琵琶视为现今最优越的实例。

en.t: Perhaps because people today have never heard the music of antiquity, they regard Kashiwagi the Gate Guard Captain’s wagon and Prince Hotaru of the Ministry of War’s biwa as the finest examples of the present age.

units.source_text: 他们的技艺固然高明无比，但今宵听到的音乐，实在可与匹敌，足使听者惊叹。

en.t: Their skill is of course unsurpassed, but the music heard tonight truly rivals it and is enough to astonish any listener.

units.source_text: 也许是由于早先认为今宵只是小规模试演，不加重视，因而感到吃惊，亦未可知。

en.t: It may be that I was surprised because I had first thought tonight was only a small trial performance and had not taken it seriously.

units.source_text: 如此妙乐，儿子的歌声其实不配参与。

en.t: For such exquisite music, my own singing voice was in truth unworthy to join in.

units.source_text: 讲到和琴，只有前太政大臣能够随心所欲地即景奏出美妙的曲调，确是特别优越的。

en.t: As for the wagon, only the former Grand Minister could freely improvise beautiful melodies on the spot, and he was indeed especially outstanding.

units.source_text: 然而一般演奏，大都无甚特色。

en.t: But ordinary performances generally have little distinction.

units.source_text: 惟今晚所听到的，实在异常美妙啊！”

en.t: What we heard tonight, however, was truly extraordinarily beautiful.”

units.source_text: 他如此赞扬紫夫人。

en.t: In this way he praised Lady Murasaki.

units.source_text: 源氏说：“这并没有什么了不起。

en.t: Genji said, “It is nothing so remarkable.

units.source_text: 只是你夸奖罢了！”

en.t: You are merely praising her too much!”

units.source_text: 他心中得意，脸上露出笑容，接着说道：“老实说，我所教出来的徒弟，个个都不坏呢。

en.t: Pleased inwardly, he showed a smile on his face and continued, “To tell the truth, every pupil I have trained is quite good.

units.source_text: 只有明石夫人的琵琶，是她家传，我没有帮助她。

en.t: Only Lady Akashi’s biwa is her family tradition; I did not help her with it.

units.source_text: 然而她到了这里之后，这乐器的音色似乎与前不同了。

en.t: Yet after she came here, the tone of that instrument seems to have changed from before.

units.source_text: 那年我遭意外之变，流寓远浦，最初听到她的琵琶时，便觉异常美妙。

en.t: That year, when I met with an unexpected misfortune and lived in exile on a distant shore, I thought her biwa extraordinarily beautiful from the first time I heard it.

units.source_text: 但现在又比那时高明得多了。”

en.t: But now she has become far more accomplished than she was then.”

units.source_text: 他强要把明石夫人的琵琶归功于自己，众侍女暗中好笑，互相以肘示意。

en.t: As he tried hard to take credit even for Lady Akashi’s biwa playing, the waiting women secretly found it amusing and nudged one another with their elbows.
